definitions: A modest granite boulder elevated, through sheer force of American mythology, to the structural weight of a founding document. Visitors arrive expecting a landmass and receive a rock roughly the size of a compact car, fenced, roofed, and guarded accordingly.
colloq. Proof that thiccc is not always a matter of tonnage. Sometimes it is a matter of narrative load bearing.
example: The tour guide gestured at Plymouth Rock with the solemnity usually reserved for objects considerably larger than it.
etymology: Named for the Massachusetts landing site tradition assigns to the Mayflower passengers in 1620, though the rock was not identified as THE rock in any record until 1741, over a century later, when a 94 year old church elder pointed it out from memory of what his father once told him.
caption: Plate CL., Plymouth Rock, weighing considerably less than its reputation.

socialCaptions.morning: Plymouth Rock. 350 plus years of fame on a boulder you could carry in a wheelbarrow, if you were allowed within fifty feet of it.
socialCaptions.afternoon: The rock itself never asked for any of this. It just sat there. Everything else was our idea.
socialCaptions.evening: From the archives, Rock, Plymouth. A landmark held to a higher standard of significance than of size.
socialCaptions.reels: Everyone expects a boulder. They built it a cage instead.
